This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1–4} Many of the exegetes said: the prepositional phrase (al-jar wa al-majrur) is linked to the surah before it; that is, We did what We did to the people of the Elephant for the sake of Quraysh, for their security, for the soundness of their affairs, and for the smooth continuation of their journeys: in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria, for the sake of trade and gains.

So Allah destroyed whoever intended them harm, and He magnified the matter of the Sacred House (al-Haram) and its people in the hearts of the Arabs, until they respected them, and did not obstruct them on any journey they wished to undertake. For this reason Allah commanded them to give thanks, saying: ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾; that is, let them single Him out and devote worship sincerely to Him, ﴿Who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾. Abundance of provision and security from fear are among the greatest worldly blessings that call for thanksgiving to Allah, the Exalted. So to You, O Allah, belongs all praise and thanks for Your blessings, both apparent and hidden. Allah singled out the Lordship over the House for its excellence and honour; otherwise, He is the Lord of everything.
